# Roadmap

## Goals

### C01 One clear owner for each relay step; no step lives in two tools

### C02 Keep the outer session's context small by moving deterministic work out of it

### C03 Use slicer and adjudicate only through their CLIs and JSON output

### C04 Follow slicer's relay contract by version, never by copying its text

### C10 One dashboard across projects: roadmaps, decisions and live relays with every agent, stage and progress

### C11 Edit and reorder the roadmap from the dashboard, every edit a slicer CLI call

### C12 Manage the decision queue from the dashboard, every change an adj CLI call made as the owner

### C13 Set up, launch and supervise parallel slice waves across vendors, owner-attended at checkpoints

### C14 User experience first: colorful, keyboard-driven TUI with mouse support

### C15 Small explicit state: ork owns only its registry, run records and UI preferences

### C18 Deterministic before model: tests, slicer check, fingerprint and report shape checked by ork before any model review

## Non-goals

### C05 No unattended runs; the owner attends every relay (open: adj scope.attended)

### C06 No tracking state of its own for items, slices, specs, readiness or decisions

### C07 No reading or writing .slicer/ or decisions/ files directly

### C08 No commits, pushes or merges unless the owner authorizes them for a run

### C09 Not an LLM; model work stays in the role agents

### C16 No scheduler: ork does not pick and run waves on its own

### C17 One workflow kind for now: the slice relay; no general pipeline language

A retry that starts a fresh round (no resumable session worth keeping, or after the vendor's out time passed) should start the chain at the first entry again; a retry of a paused round that holds a session may keep it. | 237 | [S257](slices/S257.md) | ork wait: block until a run changes state | M | 2 |  | Wave 6, 2026-11-02: an agent or script that steers ork from the CLI has no way to wait for a change. The orchestrator session polls ork status in a shell loop (.scratch/v11/watch.sh, zsh-only) and restarts it each time it fires. Proposed: 'ork wait [RUN] [--timeout D]' prints the status block and exits when a run's state, item or step changes, a question is pending, or no run is active; exit code says which. The daemon already pushes snapshots to the TUI, so the CLI can reuse them. Owner decision needed on the exit codes and on --json. Related: S237 (answer and retry return at once), S233 (ork ai guide), S240 (status text clarity). · discovered from S235 | done |
| 238 | [S258](slices/S258.md) | Spec check row: ork picks it by a setting, offers the fix when it is missing, and keeps it out of the lineups | M | 2 |  | 2026-11-03: (1) A wave launch on the slicer project failed with 'internal: the matrix has no Spec check row: add a rule that names it as Spec check row (rNN)'. The matrix had no such rule; the owner had me add r18 and rule u10 there. The adjudicate, daystar, pitfight and squalify matrices have none either (read from their relay-roles files; use 'slicer relay-roles show --root' to confirm). The message is prefixed 'internal:' although the owner can fix it, and the TUI offers no fix: it could show the exact add and rule-add commands, or a setup step in the S251 settings pane. (2) Ork finds the row only through a rule that matches Spec check row (rNN) (internal/slicercli/write.go:254), and skips only that row, the UI pass row and unknown agents when it builds the reviewer and gate chains (internal/daemon/runs.go:381-405). A second spec-check row on a vendor ork runs (for example a terra row, owner request 2026-11-03) would leak into the reviewer and gate chains and cannot be picked for the spec check. Needed: a way to choose among spec-check rows (a project setting or a note marker on the row), and every spec-check row skipped from the chains. The owner decides the marker. Related: S116, S167, S251. · discovered from S116 | done |
| 239 | [S259](slices/S259.md) | S235 later notes: guard the watchdog against a sleep detector never started, and test that the daemon starts it | S | 1 |  | From the S235 review and gate (2026-11-03), both later: (1) The daemon builds its sleep detector (Wake) once and starts it in recoverRuns. If the start is ever missed, only the watchdog's 30s tick samples the clock (internal/engine/watchdog.go:27). That equals the 30s sleep threshold (internal/engine/wake.go:25), so a tick that arrives slightly late counts 25s as sleep and a silent role could take hours to be killed. PLAUSIBLE: traced by reading, not run. Production starts it today (internal/daemon/runs.go:210). Fix: give the threshold a margin over the tick, for example 2 minutes, or count sleep only after Start has run. (2) No test fails if the Wake Start call at internal/daemon/runs.go:210 is removed; TestStatusCarriesWorkingForARunningRun checks only that both projects share one detector (internal/daemon/runs_test.go:2466). Also: 'ork projects set' refuses while any run is unfinished, so the owner could not fix the config mid-wave; a stopped run counts as unfinished. | done |
| 271 | [S294](slices/S294.md) | Fix rounds: pause and ask when they make no progress, and pause after round 3 instead of stopping at 8 | M | 2 |  | 2026-11-05, prism-ui: runs ork-20261105-160022-7f6e (U41) and -03e0 (U30) each ran 8 implementer rounds against a check that could not pass (MSB1009 from the wrong directory, S293); from round 2 the implementer reported no change and blamed the check; all 16 check logs are byte-identical. Wanted: default cap 4 (DefaultMaxRounds, internal/engine/engine.go:26, not configurable per project or run); pause into Needs you after round 3 with options (more rounds, change the check, stop); pause at once when a round changed nothing and the check output repeats byte for byte. Related: S279, S293. · discovered from S293 | done |
| 272 | [S295](slices/S295.md) | Check command: verify it once where it will run, at projects set and at run setup | M | 2 |  | 2026-11-05, prism-ui: both check commands the owner set (dotnet build PrismUi.slnx ...) were wrong from the worktree root, and nothing noticed until U41 and U30 burned 8 rounds each on MSB1009. Wanted: at run or wave setup and in 'ork projects set --check', verify the command in the exact directory the check will use and say so, with the command and directory, before any role starts. Bounded cost: a full check at setup is too slow. ork doctor already parses with sh -n and resolves the first word (internal/cli/doctor.go:171-210), but only for the main checkout and not the files the command names. Not S293 (which directory); this validates it. · discovered from S293 | done |
| 273 | [S296](slices/S296.md) | Resume a stopped run from its worktree, and continue at the stage it stopped | M | 2 |  | 2026-11-05, prism-ui: ork retry on ork-20261105-160022-7f6e (U41, stopped by the round limit) answered 'run is not paused with a pending step; use ork stop' (internal/daemon/runs.go:1015-1020). The way on was ork dismiss and a new ork run, which reused the worktree with the work (DocBuildTests.cs still there; ensureWorktree, internal/engine/states.go:705-741). Wanted: ork retry (or ork resume) of a stopped run that reloads the project settings, grants N more rounds and continues from the worktree. | 274 | [S297](slices/S297.md) | ork show RUN [NAME]: print the pause reason, a role report and the check logs, with --json | M | 2 |  | 2026-11-05, prism-ui: run ork-20261105-173816-e0c2 (U32) paused on report shape; the reviewer's report could not be read through ork. ork status prints the pause reason and no findings; ork status --json carries run fields and roles[].report names but no report text, checks or pending role and round; ork help lists no command that prints a report. The only way was the file under ~/.local/state/ork/runs/RUN/, outside the folders a coding agent may read. The daemon already has run.report (S176) for the TUI; no CLI command calls it. | 275 | [S298](slices/S298.md) | Report-shape pauses: name the real defect, feed it back to the role, and cap the retry loop | M | 2 |  | 2026-11-05, prism-ui: run ork-20261105-173816-e0c2 (U32) paused on report shape three times in a row; each ork retry re-ran the reviewer (about 3 minutes, three rounds) and the next report failed the same check. Cause: an [owner] finding fails if any line besides Options, the options and Recommend sits under its tag (internal/engine/kinds.go:133-187 into internal/engine/report.go:182-240: 5 to 7 lines, Recommend last), and the error text says Options and Recommend are missing when they are present. Nothing counts or caps consecutive shape pauses. Related: S297 (show the report), S294, S275, S287, S288. | done |
| 276 | S299 | Vendor out marks: an owner's mark survives a daemon restart and can end at a set time (--until) | S | 1 |  | Waves 7-8, 2026-11-05 (friction F43): the owner's ork vendor out grok mark was lost three times, once by a daemon restart and twice silently when the daemon idled out (daemon_idle_minutes effective 10) while a wave start was held on a spec question waiting for the owner. The next run put Grok on the reviewer row and stopped (reviewer round 1 exited unclassified), costing a full implementer round (about 28 min) each time. Fact: an owner mark has no expiry (internal/daemon/vendors.go:30-31) but lives only in daemon memory; ork vendor list after the idle exit printed 'no vendor is out'. Needed: owner marks (ork vendor out) are written to ork's state directory and reloaded at daemon start, so they end only with ork vendor back; automatic rate-limit and credit marks keep their own expiry (S273). The help text 'a restart clears them' changes to match. Related: S273, S169, S182. Absorbed from S273 (retired into this row 2026-11-07): Owner 2026-11-03: the codex weekly limit message said it resets 7:12 AM on 4 Nov, but ork vendor out takes no end time, so the mark lasts until ork vendor back (or, today, a daemon restart). Still needed, as part of this row: (a) ork vendor out VENDOR --until TIME sets an owner mark that ends at TIME, is persisted with the other owner marks, and is shown with its end time in the footer and ork vendor list; (b) reading a reset time from the vendor's own message is done only once a real captured message with a reset time exists as a test fixture; until then automatic marks keep their fixed expiry (MarkOut sets Until to at plus VendorOutFor, internal/engine/vendors.go:162; owner marks have none, MarkOutOwner at internal/engine/vendors.go:172-182). Do not write a parser against a guessed message shape. · discovered from S280 | done |

A plain relaunch passed. Fact: TestSpecCheckStopsOnPermissionDenials (internal/engine/speccheck_test.go:179) pins the stop; the spec check already retries once on a shape error (internal/engine/speccheck.go:147). Needed: a spec check whose round ended with denied read commands and no report is resumed once in the same session with the denials named and the allowed command forms from the brief's Done when section (S277); a second denial fails the check as today. One occurrence so far; S277's Done when may already prevent it. Related: S277, S266, S275. · Merged into S266 (same spec-check retry loop, speccheck.go:144-156): the denial case and what to re-check after S277 are in S266's findings. · discovered from S278 | retired |

| 287 | [S409](slices/S409.md) | Runnable Check lines | S | 1 |  | 2026-11-17: the spec check flagged orchestrator-only Check lines on S402, S396, S397, S390, S332 and S388, the same question as adj 249, 255, 256 and 259. Two causes: `checkCommandRunnable` (`internal/engine/brief.go:546-552`) treats any `;\|&<>` or backtick or `$` as a compound command even inside quotes, so `go test ./internal/daemon -run 'A\|B' -v` is orchestrator-only, while `plainCheckSyntax` (`internal/engine/brief.go:486-522`), which decides what ork itself runs, already accepts a quoted `\|`. And `ImplementerPreset` (`internal/engine/perm.go:45-71`) has no `rg` entry, so every `rg -n ...` Check line is orchestrator-only. | done |
